messages:
ajay: Quick heads-up — I ran a 200-run profiling sweep on staging after the kernel-selector change. Seeing 15–25% token latency regression on long-route (multiturn-chat) paths. Uploading traces.

perf-bot: perf report uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/perf/1767550000 (flamegraph + stage breakdown)

elaine: can you paste the flamegraph summary? which stage dominates? queue vs kernel vs kv?

ajay: kernel_exec up ~18% on 2048-token sequences. But KV_LOOKUP also spikes for warmed cache miss patterns — looks like chunked-KV hot-key thrashing when batch shapes vary.

samir: did selector start choosing dense kernels for those sequence shapes? we pushed the "kernel_v4_selector" yesterday.

ajay: yes. selector picks v4 for >1024, but v4 uses different tiling and has a new internal variant we call `k=v4_highseq`. That variant's memory layout increases per-token overhead in our measurement.

kevin: wondering if metric labels are hiding this — our `rw_token_latency_ms` currently only has `kernel_version` but not `kernel_variant` or `batch_shape`. need finer labels for debugging but careful on cardinality.

zoe: +1. we had too many ad-hoc labels in metrics-schema before and it exploded. We need a plan that lets us add debugging labels without permanent cardinality growth.

elaine: proposal: introduce ephemeral "breadcrumbs" label set for perf-debug pipelines. When `perf_debug_breadcrumbs` flag is on for X% of traffic, emit extra labels prefixed with `dbg_` and route those metrics to a high-cardinality short-retention store only (7d).

samir: love it. also add a `label_signature` field (sha256 hash of the sorted dbg label set) to correlate traces without storing all raw values in the long-term store.

ajay: concrete metric names and labels suggestion:
- `rw_token_latency_ms` (labels: route, model, kernel_version, seq_len_bucket)
- `rw_token_latency_dbg_ms` (labels: route, model, dbg_kernel_variant, dbg_batch_shape, dbg_label_sig)
Keep the `dbg` metric on 7d retention and a separate ingest path. Regular metric stays low-cardinality and long retention.

kevin: add rule: any `dbg_*` labels have a cardinality cap of 5k distinct values per day, enforced at ingestion. If exceeded, drop dbg labels and emit `dbg_sampled_count` counter.

ops-bot: rollout plan created: https://infra.redwood.internal/rollouts/1767550000 — feature flag `perf_debug_breadcrumbs` -> canary 1% -> 10% -> 100% with auto-rollback on SLO breach.

zoe: dashboard changes: create token-latency breakdown panel with stacked bars (queue_wait_ms, kv_lookup_ms, kernel_exec_ms, encode_decode_ms). Add per-route KPI card showing p50/p95/p99 and `regressed_since` annotation. Also add a short-lived dbg-dashboard that surfaces `rw_token_latency_dbg_ms` with sample traces.

elaine: migration notes: rename old metric `token_latency_v1` -> mark deprecated and alias for 30d -> new canonical `rw_token_latency_ms` with label `schema=v2`. During rollout collect both metrics and run a 72h backfill for critical routes.

samir: question: how to annotate archived traces? keep breadcrumb traces for 7d only, but persist `label_signature` -> mapping records for 30d so we can resolve dbg hashes to human-readable variants when investigating long-tail regressions.

ajay: action items:
- ajay: produce flamegraphs + example dbg payload (by EOD)
- elaine: PR for metric names + ingestion guards (metrics repo)
- kevin: implement cardinality throttle in metric pipeline (ingest-service)
- zoe: dashboard PR (grafana/dashboards)
- samir: add `label_signature` hashing util and docs
I'll open follow-up threads for each.

kevin: ack. I'll start a small load test comparing selector v3 vs v4 with representative batch-shapes.

perf-bot: CI perf-check scheduled: https://ci.redwood.internal/perf/checks/1767550000 — baseline vs canary run queued.

zoe: thanks team :thumbsup:

ajay: if anyone hits the flamegraph link and sees different hotspots, paste the exact sample id. small differences matter (tile size vs memory copy pattern).
